## Farm removal native entry points

The diagnostic `df3d farm-contents-read <farm>` returns contained items in native
vector order, with IDs, roles, flags, native Dump/Melt eligibility and captions.
Captions call the common building-sheet formatter c65450(item, owned string,
false, -1), as renderer19d4ae does. Its complete relocation-free body spans two
unwind entries through c65f0a (length0xaba, FNV47fa672b7bbcd332); checking only
the first entry misses the decoration logic. Direct global reads concern game
mode, installed display settings and world records, not native menu scratch.
DFHack's decorated getDescription reconstructs formatting and is not this call.

Protected native221721 on2026-10-28 verifies40 permanent seed rows and matches
the first six captions verbatim against native screen cells at baseline and
after both directions of Forbid/Dump/Visibility. Reads preserve all observed
item facts and byte-for-byte view_sheets/plotinfo state. The owned paused
DF180196 exits unsaved and the source-save manifest is unchanged. Evidence is
retained in `native_farm.json.contents_reader_reference`. Other item types,
quality/wear/artifact captions, tail scrolling and active jobs remain unverified.
This establishes the native reader. Its management-wire transport is described
below; Godot controls remain unfinished and the farm route stays staged.

Management88 transports explicit `ProductionInspect` reads with `contents=true`.
The current producer supports visible farm plots; the page contract is reusable
for other buildings after native acceptance. It returns ordered semantic rows,
native UTF-8 captions, role, item flags, eligibility and job/building indicators.
Contents revisions remain independent of farm crop settings. A page contains
at most64 rows and128KiB of encoded captions. Continuations carry the complete
contents revision; changed contents reject without an authoritative page. Empty
contents have an explicit empty page; missing historical data remains unknown.
The shared page builder measures converted strings, preserves order and rejects
an individually oversized row rather than truncating it or reporting completion.

Existing crop/header reads and native-menu guards remain covered. All seven

oversized caption refusal. Codec tests reject malformed/mixed pages and preserve
revisions above2^53. This is read transport acceptance, not rendered contents UI
or typed item-write acceptance. The native item transaction and its separate
wire acceptance follow below.

Management89 carries ItemForbid/ItemDump/ItemMelt/ItemHidden as explicit
FarmEdit operations with item ID, desired value and exact contents revision.
These carry no season/crop/fertilizer/name fields. The native transaction
re-finds the target and observes fresh contents after execution. Completed
replies include a bounded page starting at the affected item and a typed receipt
with matching item/operation/value. Validation requires a completed,
non-removing building and the observed desired flag in that page. Rejected,
Stale and Unknown replies grant no contents authority; uncertain effects are
never replayed. This transport currently targets farm plots and remains staged.

`building_contents_state.gd` owns one bounded contents page and local request
generation. It preserves native row order and exact revisions, validates page
boundaries and semantic fields, and returns isolated rows to views. Seeking
retires obsolete queued/sent observers; it never combines different revisions.
Edits send explicit desired values without optimistic flag changes. A confirmed
receipt replaces old authority; if it begins at the clicked row, a read at the
new revision recovers the previous page offset. Rejected/Stale/Unknown outcomes
clear authority and never replay writes. Close cancels queued work and detaches
sent work; session changes retire identity and tickets. It is not yet connected
to the rendered farm sheet.

harness uses the existing service bootstrap path. It is not earlier controller
acceptance. `contents_controller_reference` retains final evidence. Actual
transport-loss/producer-replacement and rendered retirement remain separate gaps.

## Staged farm contents presentation

The farm owner now opens and retires a separate bounded contents controller.
Confirmed farm/item edits refresh the other snapshot through reads; no optimistic
item flags are drawn. Removal hides and retires contents, while closing the
sheet or losing the session clears rows and drag state. The native row component
uses installed seed artwork, picture/background cells and Stocks item controls.
Forbid, Dump and Visibility submit explicit desired values with current identity
and revision; native eligibility governs the Melt/Dump controls. The View icon
currently emits an item identity only: its item sheet remains unfinished.

also verifies explicit action/eligibility routing, owner/pending gates and empty

checks cleanly and both contents/sheet GPU checks with the three known Godot

route remains hidden; other management screens and release work remain pending.

## Farm contents short lists and cell scrolling

Native contents scrolls in12-pixel cells, three per item. Renderer19cda1 subtracts
`scroll_position_item` from the cell origin, and19e0aa supplies page*3 and count*3-1
to native scrollbar initializer bb380. Its inclusive range calculation in bb3b0
therefore measures cells, not items. DF3D retains cell position locally and uses
floor(cell/3) for semantic contents paging; crossing an item boundary reads that
page, while within-item scrolling needs no round trip. Partially visible rows keep
clipped backgrounds/text/controls, but seed artwork appears only for complete rows.
No native presentation state or graphics cache is used by the runtime.

Protected native000849 on2026-10-29 supplies initial/scroll-cell1/2/3/47 captures
and controlled7/6/1/0-item lists. It preserves allocations and restores all original
membership pointers/order; source-save preservation passes and DF175292 exits

The current runtime still has this gap: observeFarmItem and item edits depend on
original farm membership and the whole farm contents revision. Background
inspection therefore retires a still-existing transferred item. Do not treat
this as native parity or weaken only the membership guard. Item identity,
revision and actions need independent ownership, with location links represented
separately from the original containing farm.

separate from holder rows. Existing nativeStockpileAt uses generica82b00, whose reverse scan and extra
occupancy filtering differ from the item renderer. The independent native helper
below follows the item renderer; management transport/UI migration remains pending.

## Independent native item observation and edits

`observeItem(item)` now supplies item-owned facts, native caption/weight/description,
building-holder and spatial-stockpile links, and an item-specific revision.
It retains the audited seed/bar description allowlist and uses native effective
position/visibility and extent predicates. Stockpile names call native getName.
It never reads view_sheets or uses the former containing farm as authority.
Building contents share the extracted ItemFacts reader and retain their separate
membership, role, build-state and whole-contents revision contract.

`ItemObservation` revisions cover item facts, eligibility, job references, native
text and location links, including link names. Follow coordinates remain separate
from edit authority. `finishItemEdit` requires the exact observed revision, checks
native eligibility, and confirms the same item and requested flag in a fresh
receipt. Stale/unconfirmed outcomes confer no receipt; uncertain entry is never
replayed. Location changes do not themselves invalidate a confirmed same-item
receipt. Repeated desired values return existing authority without mutation.
The diagnostic commands are `item-inspect-probe <item>` and
`item-flag-probe <item> <forbid|dump|melt|hidden> <0|1> <revision>`.

then carries the semantic kind, ID, native name and container item type through

are mutually exclusive; a spatial stockpile remains independent. A carrier change
or rename invalidates the prior revision. Unit links require item type -1;
container types require0..92. Invalid kinds, IDs, text or conflicting holders grant
no authority. Version94 peers are incompatible; missing historical relationships
remain unknown. Artwork and navigation integration remain separate work.

a complete observation and exact revision. Rename accepts at most30 losslessly

execution. Successful effects require a fresh valid observation with matching
identity/stages and the requested change. Rejected/Stale/Unknown grant no receipt;
post-entry exceptions or unverifiable effects are Unknown and never replayed.
Transport callers must additionally validate the world epoch and target visibility.

them. This removes the observed readback warnings without changing native art.

agreement dispatches. Their index bounds, optional byte remaps and target RVAs
were checked against the enclosing indexed bodies. No traversed instruction
intersects those table ranges. All eight candidate writes in the older
`event-write-candidates.json` fall inside dispatch data, including the apparent
`movsb` at b76544; they are not evidence of source mutation.

The traversed roots have 49 distinct direct callees and 16 non-import indirect
call sites. All 97 outgoing direct tail edges reach the existing date formatter
b92640. No unresolved jump remains in this root-level traversal, but callees,
virtual targets, source aliases and transitively referenced storage are separate
ownership obligations. Both masterpiece-lost b65093 and performance b8c43b invoke another event's
phrase slot d8. Their recursive event/source ownership remains a production
admission obligation.

### Knowledge coin-caption source requirements

The artifact dependency is broader than ARTIFACT_CREATED. The supported
executable's audited event roots contain22 direct calls to b94400 across19
event types: agreement concluded/formed; artifact claim formed, copied,
created, destroyed, dropped, found, given, hidden, lost, possessed, recovered,
stored and transformed; HF act on artifact, HF learns secret, historical
figure died and item stolen. ARTIFACT_TRANSFORMED formats both new_artifact
and entries from old_artifact; validating only its first artifact is insufficient.
Agreement detail payloads and death/theft item resolution require separate
dependency extraction, rather than treating all these events as a common
artifact_id layout. Eight event roots also call circumstance helper b5a6c0.
Its second dispatch maps unit thoughts AcquireArtifact236 and GaveArtifact239
to b5b594/b5b5b6, then calls b94400 using the fifth argument, circumstance
data. These are additional dependencies even when an event's primary artifact
has already passed validation. The shared diagnostic traversal checks them for
ARTIFACT_CLAIM_FORMED, ARTIFACT_GIVEN, ARTIFACT_POSSESSED, ENTITY_DISSOLVED,
HF_GAINS_SECRET_GOAL and ITEM_STOLEN. CHANGE_HF_MOOD/CHANGE_HF_STATE instead
pass constant-1 for the circumstance and need no artifact extraction here.
The generated circumstance union lacks an artifact-named member; the adapter
copies its four-byte payload after checking the exact thought type, without
changing DFHack's generated structures. The local artifact-event-dependencies.json
records call sites and instruction neighborhoods against executable SHA256
205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7;
the neighborhoods are not a transitive dataflow proof.

Agreement artifact extraction follows the native first-detail dispatch.
FORMED table2afde4 maps PlotStealArtifact6 to2ae859 (artifact_id at payload0xc,
call2ae964), and RetrieveArtifact17 to2afc7d (artifact at payload8,
call2afd7e). CONCLUDED tableb83148 maps only RetrieveArtifact17 to the
artifact callb82f05; its PlotStealArtifact branch emits generic plot text.

### Knowledge detail request ownership

`creature_knowledge_state.gd` owns one on-demand detail ticket. Pending duplicate
selection shares that ticket; a different unit, native kind or entry cancels
queued work or detaches sent work and immediately clears old text. Callbacks
must match the owner's generation, ticket and complete response/request
identity. Ready requires the successful envelope and bounded tagged text;
Rejected/Unavailable never retain text. Closing, disposal, epoch changes,
same-epoch session replacement and confirmed transport loss retire authority.
Timeout consumes the observer without retry; a later success cannot reopen the
detail. Reconnection may let the shared service claim a catalog, but never
replays the retired detail request. No new player-visible status copy is added.

`knowledge-owner-final` passes root/core and the headless owner test using the
real semantic request service with an injected transport. It covers all four
native kinds, queued/sent close, duplicate/replacement selection, late replies,
malformed identity/types, contradictory outcomes, UTF-8 byte limits, timeout,
epoch/session/disconnect/reconnect and disposal. The final Godot log is clean.
Earlier lifecycle testing corrected the mock's transport-loss signal and a
NUL-check implementation that emitted Unicode parsing diagnostics; those runs
are not clean acceptance. Byte-level NUL rejection remains independently tested
by the wire codec. The owner is attached to the staged creature sheet as described
below. No UI exposure or live native request acceptance follows from this
isolated controller check.

## Seed item inspection transport

Management91 uses ProductionInspect with building_id and item_id for an item
inspection. It excludes contents paging, revision preconditions and edit fields.
BuildingItemSnapshot contains the post-format contents revision, building state,
owned item facts, weight, description and optional ItemBuildingHolder. Missing
historical snapshots and absent holders remain absent. Validators bound every
string, require identity and reject mixed or unsuccessful authority. PINS.md
records the breaking migration; both bridge and viewer must be rebuilt together.

Bridge encoding, neutral decoding and Godot dictionary conversion are implemented.
The runtime provider validates visible farm membership and exact seed/bar dispatch
before native entry. It returns native description, weight, holder identity and
contents facts observed after formatting. Missing targets and other item types
are rejected without falling through to the legacy building inspector. Native
weight calculation and the semantic historical-figure-to-creature cache may be
initialized; native menu/viewscreen state is not used. This does not enable the
public item sheet or authorize generic item-description calls.

2^53, absent holders, malformed requests and bounded snapshots. MSVC passes.

DF174204 exits unsaved; two save manifests stay unchanged. The diagnostic primitive

`item_sheet_state.gd` owns one inspection target and snapshot through the shared
semantic action service. Flag edits use the exact inspected revision and native
eligibility. Its independent snapshot has no original-building identity or

Closing cancels queued requests and detaches sent observers. Stale, rejected and
unknown edits discard authority and require explicit refresh; no edit is replayed.
Holder and stockpile links are independently validated and replaced on refresh.
Building contents retain their separate revision and receipt contract.

## Effective item position transport

Management92 adds `ProductionInspect` with `locate_item=true` and `item_id`.
This request excludes building identity, contents, paging, revision preconditions
and edits. It resolves the item independently of farm membership through DF's
native `itemFollowPosition` adapter. Missing, removed, invalid-coordinate and
hidden-terrain targets reject without position authority. The adapter resolves
effective position through `itemPosition`, then calls DF's designation reader
for the follow visibility guard. A successful `production.item_position`
contains only the requested ID and effective map coordinate. Schema validators
reject mixed authority and out-of-range coordinates; absent historical positions
stay absent. Neither the request nor the result carries camera or follow state.
Bridge and viewer must use management92 together, as recorded in PINS.md.

pass, including boolean/ID types, forbidden mixed fields, absent positions and
typed Vector3i conversion. MSVC passes. Protected144812 verifies forty native
position comparisons, missing-ID rejection, fresh coordinates after a controlled
move, removed-item rejection and exact restoration, alongside existing item
inspection/edit/controller regressions. Native UI guards and both save manifests
remain unchanged; DF181580 exits unsaved. `item_position_wire_reference` retains
provenance. This transport does not establish natural hauling. Viewer following
uses the owned controller below, without native camera or menu state.

The staged `item_follow.gd` controller owns an item independently of its sheet.
It serializes position reads with a 100ms delay after each receipt, emits only
changed positions, and fences late replies by ticket and generation. Closing the
sheet preserves following; a repeated camera click, manual pan, explicit focus,
elevation navigation or entering Walk stops it. Session invalidation and rejected
positions retire the target without retry. The item owner reflects this identity
using the installed active/inactive camera artwork.

name, a nonempty native-formatted caption and all non-name semantic facts
unchanged. Exceptions or unverifiable post-effect receipts yield Unknown with
no completion authority; false from the apply callback must mean no effects.

converter tests alone do not establish actual DF conversion or live effects.

The controller owns single intents; `farm_rename_session.gd` owns a stream of

### Native farm transport contract

Management85 adds required custom/header names and removal, suspended and worker
facts to FarmSnapshot. The safe-point reader obtains them from `farmHeader`;
world model and Godot receive owned values. All five fields participate in the
content revision, so name/status changes invalidate earlier edit receipts.
Wire and controller validators reject absent/oversized names, empty captions and
removal flags on a farm not marked for removal. Old versions cannot synthesize
these facts or new revisions; bridge and viewer must migrate together.

### Native farm presentation controller

`farm_state.gd` owns target/tab selection, receipt authority and display order
through the shared semantic action service. Initial open reads the current
native season before exposing a tab. Edits carry the exact displayed revision
with one outstanding intent and no optimistic effect. Fresh successful snapshots
retain their provider order and revision unchanged; a separate row-ID list keeps
native entry positions stable until a tab rebuild. Choices always come from the
latest native snapshot. No seed or growth eligibility is reconstructed here.

Closing/changing target detaches old tickets: queued writes are canceled;
sent writes drain through the service without reviving the old observer.
Rejected, Stale and Unknown clear usable snapshot authority. Explicit recovery
reads fresh facts and never replays a write. Epoch loss retires the target.
The shared service now classifies typed FarmEditOutcome.Unknown as detached
uncertainty, consistent with its existing area/construction handling.

initialization, queued/sent tab retirement, stable post-edit row order,
crop/fertilizer effects, an external native crop change causing a stale refusal,
fresh-read recovery, and invalid-target retirement. Six observed completions
and nine native checks preserve paused frame/menu/tab state; both save manifests
are unchanged and DF176504 exits unsaved. The result is clean and recorded in
`native_farm.json.controller_reference`. The first171739 attempt omitted the
new action service's bootstrap Catalog claim and is not acceptance.

This is headless controller acceptance. Native panel rendering, installed
artwork, actual map-selection integration, and real disconnect/replacement
tests remain unfinished. The farm screen is not exposed.

`location_recognition_state.gd` owns the recognition receipt independently of
Details. It retains the prior display during apply, accepts one explicit intent,
validates reply action/operation/target/revision, and publishes only confirmed
snapshots. Stale, rejected and unknown responses clear the actionable receipt;
none automatically retries. A malformed successful mutation is Unknown. Closing
cancels unsent work and detaches sent work; generation checks prevent late replies
from reviving or retargeting the owner. Session changes retire it.

`location_recognition_workflow.gd` coordinates that owner with Details. A ready
temple observation starts a recognition read for that exact Details lifetime and
revision. Applying excludes other Details edits; confirmed completion refreshes
Details/staff, while an unknown result releases unrelated controls without replay.
Changing target, closing or another Details operation retires the old recognition
owner. Details now connects this coordinator to `location_recognition_view.gd`.
`build/qa/location-recognition-workflow` exercises the real semantic action service
with a controlled producer, including exact >2^53 revision handling, no optimistic
changes, stale/unknown refusal, unsent cancellation, late success, epoch changes,
malformed successful replies and the Details edit/refresh boundary. It is a clean
headless pass, not rendered or real-disconnect acceptance. Root/core evidence is
`build/qa/location-recognition-controller-core`.

## Native zone owner assignment audit

Owner picker client-loss coverage runs through `areas_acceptance.ps1
-ControllerScene -ZoneOwnerOnly -OwnerDisconnect queued|sent`. It uses an actual
visible candidate click and checks its queued owner ID. The sent case waits for
its own sequence behind background reads, observes DF completion without
delivering the receipt, then disconnects. Queued work retires as not_sent;
sent work retires as unknown. Both clear picker authority, reconnect without
replaying area work, and explicitly reopen through the Zones launcher and map.
Fresh selection and native snapshots agree on the unapplied/applied owner;
the picker reopens and dismisses, and the zone is removed through the UI.

`build/qa/owner-disconnect-reopen`. Initial150330 clicked before container layout
settled and targeted another row; it is not acceptance. The test now uses the

## Multi Undo native cleanup

Normal Multi Undo now uses the verified zone cleanup helpers with owned overlap
scratch. Its native handler0x34cb5f..0x34cc58 iterates history forward, calls
removal for each entry, clears history/counters and returns without a final
overlap refresh. This differs from ordinary-panel removal: Multi retains the
pre-retirement overlap observation for each deletion. The bridge preserves that
timing through ZoneRemovalKind::MultiUndo, without reading native history or
borrowing native map search arrays. Its existing scoped receipt still validates
the complete target set before deleting anything and consumes authority before
mutation. Compatibility rejection occurs before consuming that receipt.

path_cost/path_tag guards. Existing native reference checks cover room defaults,
footprints, furniture links, mixed sets, stale targets and foreign scopes.

## Owner display observation contract

Management63 adds optional `AreaCandidateRow.owner_display` for scoped owner
candidate replies. It carries native first/second name lines, room-status text,
room value and formatting width in columns. Width is bounded to3..128; text
limits are384 UTF-8 bytes per name line and256 for status. A zero room value
requires empty status; positive values require a status. Other candidate kinds
must not carry this record. Missing records in older recordings remain unknown,
not empty native rows. This migration establishes transport only; production
reader and renderer integration is verified in the native owner audit above.

Management64 adds optional `AreaOwnerDisplay.name_color`: two owned foreground,
background and brightness triplets plus effect0..3 (steady, legendary, nemesis,
fire). Foreground/background are palette indices0..7; brightness is0..1. Steady
records require identical alternatives. The record adds seven bytes to bounded
payload accounting. Missing records remain unknown, including historical owner
rows with text but no color. No clock, RNG, native pointer or renderer state is
transported. This contract change does not itself connect the production reader
or authorize exposing the staged picker.

`build/qa/owner-color-contract` passes root CTest19/19 and the real Godot
contract decoder, including both color alternatives and their effect. Boundary
checks reject out-of-range components/effects and unequal steady alternatives;
missing historical color records remain absent.

Management65 adds optional `AreaCandidateRow.sheet_icon`, an owned original-asset
recipe using SelectionAppearance. It is restricted to owner CandidateList rows
with nonnegative IDs. Each recipe has at most256 page names, palettes and layers;
page/palette text limits are256/512 bytes. Layer references must resolve within
that recipe, with nonzero cell dimensions. Recipe strings and layers count
against the existing224KiB area-response payload limit. Missing historical
recipes remain absent; they are never inferred from names or map visibility.
Godot receives page names, palette names and ten integer values per layer in
schema order, preserving signed palette rows and offsets. This establishes the
transport; production integration and scoped native-image parity are verified
in the owner audit above. The owner picker remains staged pending full acceptance.
`build/qa/owner-icon-contract-fixed` passes root CTest19/19 and the real Godot
contract test. It checks lossless recipe decoding, historical absence, wrong
operation/kind, invalid indices/cell sizes, per-recipe caps and aggregate payload
limits. These transport tests do not establish native image parity.

Bridge, model and Godot must be rebuilt together. The current contract region is
`Local\df3d_management_v65`; version64 peers cannot share it. The installed
development plugin and current viewer both use version65.
Historical version62 evidence below describes the earlier overlap migration.

`build/qa/owner-display-contract-final` passes root CTest19/19 and the Godot
contract check. Coverage includes native lines through the real engine decoder,
absent legacy records, invalid widths/value/status/scope and an explicit old
version. Live producer acceptance is recorded in the native owner audit above.

## Native single-zone allocation and registration

Single-zone creation uses DF's factory0x28b650, completion0x577040,

## Native stockpile links (DF 53.16)

Run `tools/smoke/stockpile_storage_native.ps1 -Links` for the protected pointer
oracle. `fixtures/areas/native_stockpile_links.json` retains exact endpoint and
picker observations plus native code hashes from the supported binary.

Escape, stockpile/workshop give and take, duplicates, reversal and removal.
Source hashes were unchanged, simulation stayed paused and owned DF closed unsaved.

Native permits one direction per pair. Choosing the opposite direction replaces
both reciprocal links; it does not create a bidirectional pair. Self-selection
and an already-present direction leave the picker open without mutation. A new
link returns to the list; Escape cancels the picker. Removal updates both ends.
The bridge prepares owned copies of both endpoints and calls the pinned native
lookup, insertion and erasure routines. Reversal removes the opposite links;
duplicate selection leaves the endpoints unchanged. Both endpoints are published
after preparation. Capacity is reserved before native insertion so its allocator
branch is not entered. The former local two-vector editor has been removed.
The picker retains duplicate/self selection without showing a self-link error.
The public workflow uses these native link operations.

Native target handler `0x3c2a70` reads global link UI despite taking an interface
pointer and is prohibited as a runtime service. Its stockpile pair branch uses
explicit-vector lookup `0x3c9ff0`, insertion `0xeb530` and erasure `0x3c7390`.
Workshop helpers `0x5832b0`/`0x583320` establish the reciprocal/opposite-direction
mapping; the runtime uses the same native vector primitives with owned storage.
Link commands now use explicit synchronous work accounting, retaining honest
unknown-work reporting without spending the paginated read budget. Native UI
state is not consulted. Production target selection now uses the verified native query described below.
Ordering and scoped scrolling/scaled-input acceptance are recorded below.

## Native stockpile storage input (DF 53.16)

Run `tools/smoke/stockpile_storage_native.ps1 -CloneEvidence <verified-run-folder>`
for the protected native storage oracle. The folder must contain a matching
`clone-path.txt` and `clone-manifest.txt`. The owned lane disables autosave,
remains paused, captures native pointer/keyboard effects and screenshots, closes
without saving, and verifies the source manifest. Setup changes are confined to
the disposable session; this is not DF3D gameplay acceptance.

Protected `build/stockpile-storage-native-20261025-083759` recorded108 observations
on a272-tile pile. All three fields use the occupied tile count as their ordinary
upper bound, including wheelbarrows. The number field starts blank, accepts three
digits and ignores non-digits. Accepted text changes immediately update the
stored field, clamping to the tile count; Enter only finishes entry. Backspacing
to empty writes zero. Escape closes the popup and retains already applied edits.
Opening an empty field and immediately submitting leaves the old value intact.
The fixture `native_stockpile_storage.json` retains exact input/output records,
binary-range hashes and omissions. Source save hashes were unchanged and owned
DF closed unsaved.

The staged DF3D storage surface normalizes three digits and requests clamped
values immediately. Enter finishes entry; Escape/Done closes the popup while
preserving requested writes. Closing collects any final LineEdit text change
whose notification is still deferred. Opening a blank field makes no request;
deleting existing input to empty requests zero. Accepted writes advance the
revision without clearing the entry. Newer explicit input waits for that receipt
and uses the action service's continuation queue; rejection or an unknown outcome
drops buffered input. Closing the entire panel cancels unsent work and detaches
sent work. Reopening the popup obtains a fresh inspection before enabling edits.

The native pointer path at
`0x334fa9..0x33561b` counts tiles through `0x57b770` and performs inline field
updates. The text path at `0x8ba405..0x8ba683` uses numeric input helper
`0xc39700` with length3, native containment checks and inline field conversion/
clamping. Both paths borrow native UI globals and must not be invoked as runtime
semantic services. No standalone storage mutation routine is established by this
audit. The renderer is `0x3aef70..0x3afd54`.

`AreaInfo.storage_limit` now exposes the ordinary native bound for all three
container fields. Its additive default is-1 for unavailable/legacy observations;
schema/management version56 is unchanged. The shared native tile-count service
calls the audited extent predicate at `0x5587b0`, also used by the native preset
path, without viewscreen or menu state. Snapshot work accounts for that additional
pass. The bridge validates edits against this observed bound; Godot no longer
derives the cap from geometry or subtracts one for wheelbarrows. Unknown bounds
disable storage editing. Counts outside nonnegative signed16 storage remain
unavailable; this does not claim native overflow behavior.

## Native stockpile resize storage and empty lifecycle (DF 53.16)

Use `tools/smoke/stockpile_storage_native.ps1 -Repaint` for the protected native
resize oracle. Run `build/stockpile-storage-native-repaint-20261025-100204`
recorded287 observations: a272-tile pile erased one cell at a time to one tile
clamped all three limits to the remaining occupied count on every step. Its
bounding rectangle stayed unchanged. Regrowing to two tiles retained limits of1;
limits below the new count remained unchanged. Erasing the last cell retained
the empty pile and its previous limits. Regrowth reused that identity. Accept
was disabled while empty; Escape removed the empty pile. The source save stayed
unchanged and owned DF closed unsaved. Bounded exact records and the full-result
digest are in `fixtures/areas/native_stockpile_resize.json`.

The native clamp is inline at `0x354a29..0x354acf`, inside UI handler `0x311c10`.
The preceding path checks emptiness through `0x559580`, skips the active empty
pile, and counts through `0x57b770`. This is evidence, not a callable semantic
service. The bridge now preflights parallel container vectors, uses the native
extent predicate and item assignment method to release removed assignments,
and clamps all three limits to the native count. The staged painter submits each
completed gesture through an action-service-owned session. It preserves bounds
on erase and retains an empty pile until exit. Accept is disabled while empty.
The empty area's allocated bounds must remain fully loaded and revealed for
inspection or regrowth; its occupied and visible-cell counts stay zero.
Do not treat the native oracle as acceptance of unverified product paths.

Extended protected run `build/stockpile-storage-native-repaint-20261025-100535`
tracked46 actual assigned containers through292 observations. Shrinking to one
tile released45 assignments and retained the remaining container. The empty
active pile retained that final assignment; Escape released it when removing the
pile. All46 items remained alive. Released item references became id-1 with
coordinates-30000/-30000. Source hashes were unchanged and owned DF closed
unsaved. The resize fixture retains all46 before/after item references.

The native repaint path at `0x354817..0x354943` tests each assigned coordinate,
calls item virtual slot208 (`removeStockpileAssignment`) and removes the
corresponding entry from all four storage vectors. Audited barrel/bin leaf
`0x28ad00..0x28ad15` and tool leaf `0x28a450..0x28a465` only reset fields in the
supplied item; they read no UI/global state and allocate nothing. Use this native
item operation for cleanup. `detachStockpileAssignment` is a
different operation that also changes the pile's vectors. Offline
`build/qa/stockpile-assignment-oracle` passed root CTest for that native audit.

`tools/smoke/areas_acceptance.ps1 -SaveId <new-id> -StockpileResizeOnly` runs

272 occupied tiles to one released45 of46 container assignments, retained the
matching container, preserved bounds, and clamped limits to1/1/1. Regrowth to two

parallel vector was rejected before changing geometry; a stale resize was also

This proves command effects, not the unfinished painter's gesture/empty lifecycle.
Native cleanup runs synchronously at a safe point and reports unknown work cost;

Main-scene regression `build/areas-acceptance-20261025-101902` passed124 native

CTest. This regression retains the existing deferred-commit painter; it does

Native gesture runs `build/stockpile-storage-native-gestures-*` at102921,
102947,103013 and103039 on2026-10-25 independently establish that Escape and

The generic `area_paint_session.gd` owns queued gestures and receipts independently
of panel lifetime. Initial stockpile hits resolve before any creation is sent;
finding an existing pile discards creation strokes and selects that identity.
An empty lookup releases queued strokes even after the panel closes. Rejection,
unknown outcomes and epoch changes stop the queue without replay. Successful
mutation receipts carry subsequent gestures/deletion through the service's
continuation contract. Accept sends no replacement for already applied geometry.

confirms removal; both save manifests remain unchanged and DF closes unsaved.
Its only diagnostic is the known separate-thread notice.

`area_paint_state.gd` now owns geometry only: sampled cells, rectangles, bounds,
spans and generations. Request preparation, replacement-at-Accept, local brush
interpolation and the controller's no-owner mutation fallback are removed.
The session is the sole owner of gesture submission and authoritative replies.
Queued work retains full explicit gesture spans rather than differences against
speculative cells. Identical adjacent unsent brush samples coalesce. Each reply
rebuilds preview geometry from DF's observed footprint and reapplies newer queued
intent, removing clipped ghosts without dropping later overlapping edits. If
an outstanding addition resolves to empty, pending Accept is disarmed and Paint
stays open. Unknown/rejected results still stop the owner without replay.
`build/qa/stockpile-gesture-reconcile-final` checks these clipped-reply boundaries.

success with no identity. The owner consumes that gesture without replay, retains

Offline `build/qa/stockpile-paint-cleanup-fixed` passes core, controller, geometry

## Native stockpile placement eligibility (DF 53.16)

`fixtures/areas/native_stockpile_placement.json` records native pointer rectangles
with controlled terrain/occupancy in disposable paused sessions. Reproduce with
`stockpile_storage_native.ps1 -PaintGestures -GestureCase eligibility`; creation
uses `-GestureCase eligibility-create -EligibilityCase <case>` and a fresh process
per case. The fixture records exact runs, result digests, inputs and effects.
All successful oracle sessions close unsaved with unchanged source manifests.

Native repaint trims wall, hidden, occupied and open-space cells while painting
the other selected cells. Water depths1/2/7 and magma1 remain eligible. Independent
creation runs confirm full selected bounds with holes, deep-water/magma acceptance,
and no building published for an all-wall rectangle; painting remains open.
Creation uses DF's scalar predicates and native hidden/occupancy gates to filter
its privately owned mask, preserving the full requested bounds even with invalid
edge cells. An empty mask returns success without allocating a building or ID.
Protected `build/areas-acceptance-20261025-113417` verifies nine creation cases,
including invalid edges, hidden/occupied cells, liquids and all-wall no-op, plus
the existing storage cleanup regression. It passes cleanly with unsaved closure
and two unchanged save manifests. Viewport run
`build/areas-acceptance-20261025-113545` verifies all-clipped creation keeps Paint
open with Accept disabled, then accepts a valid gesture and removal. The capture
was inspected; only the known separate-thread notice remains, with unsaved
closure and unchanged manifests.

Repaint additions filter owned spans through the same native predicates before
planning allocation bounds. Native growth probes (`eligibility-grow` with
`wall-left`, `wall-right`, `all-wall` or `floor`) establish that rejected cells
do not extend bounds; an all-rejected stroke leaves the pile unchanged. Protected
`build/areas-acceptance-20261025-114153` passes exact masks/bounds and retained-cell
checks for all four cases, plus creation and storage cleanup regressions. Owned
DF closed unsaved with two unchanged manifests.

Native `eligibility-erase` covers12 terrain/occupancy cases: erasing ignores
placement eligibility, including hidden cells. Stockpile erasure therefore
requires loaded cells but does not reject hidden cells. An empty stockpile stays
observable when at least one coordinate in its allocated bounds is revealed,
with zero visible occupied cells, so removal can follow an erase across hidden
cells. Zones retain their existing visibility policy. Protected
`build/areas-acceptance-20261025-114757` passes six invalid-cell erase cases, exact
empty extents/occupancy, unchanged bounds and subsequent deletion, plus prior
creation/growth/storage checks. Source and clone manifests are unchanged; owned

Cross-pile additions prepare donor cell indexes and validate every affected
stockpile before publishing any edit. Native owner lookup `0xa82b00` determines
the donor; retained donors use native assignment cleanup and limit clamping.
Empty donors use native removal `0x587d80(b,false,false,false)`, including
relationship cleanup and object destruction. Erasing outside the selected pile
leaves other piles unchanged, as the native partial/full erase probes establish.
Native pointer creation and repaint transfer fixtures retain exact ownership,
container assignment and donor-deletion observations.

Stockpile creation uses DF's constructor `0x30f090` (which allocates the ID and
registers the building), completion routine `0x577040` and stockpile categorize
method. Settings, extents, transfer edits and refresh allocations are prepared
before publication. Native inline bounds/number setup is reproduced with owned

existing registration path. The DFHack `setSize`/`constructAbstract` stockpile
path was removed: it rejects occupied cells even when native's pile designation
permits them. Accepted creation cells receive the native pile designation before
completion, matching the inline write at `0x3538b4..0x3538dd`. Completion alone
sets building occupancy without that designation; omitting it prevents later
paint transfers from recognizing newly created piles. Matching all317 native tile types to HighPassable was insufficient
to establish that helper's full eligibility parity.

The captures below document the native-service migration. For the current
verified construction scope, see [Construction coverage boundary](#construction-coverage-boundary).

Construction preview and placement now delegate Door wall support to DF's
coordinate-only routine at RVA `0xa827b0`. The plugin verifies the supported PE
and fingerprints the routine and its support-tile classifier before calling it
at a safe point. Unknown builds/inputs fail closed. It returns owned scalar
results and the sourced refusal `Needs adjacent wall`; Godot remains asynchronous.
No native build request, menu, cursor or redraw scratch is borrowed or changed.
The old Lua wall/fortification adjacency approximation is removed. Generic floor,
occupancy, liquid and DFHack construction checks remain; this is not full native
placement parity. Sourced Door refusal presentation is described below.

## Native removal workflows (2026-10-04)

Maintainer direction is to match native removal semantics. In the mining toolbar,
the remove-stairs/ramps/constructions tool now designates completed constructed
tiles through DFHack's native `Constructions::designateRemove`. The eraser cancels
designations, including active `RemoveConstruction` jobs; it is not a bulk ordinary
building demolition tool. Native captures and sourced tooltips are recorded in
`fixtures/construction/removal.json`.

Selecting an ordinary building now exposes DF's `BUILDING_SHEET_REMOVE` action,
then `Slated for removal` and `Cancel removal`. The existing right-click/Escape
path closes the sheet. The selection-owned controller reads authoritative state

## Picker receipt profiling and fix (2026-10-04)

Follow-up tracing found avoidable main-thread CPU work. In
`build/construction-phase-trace-20261004-023131`, viewport GPU time near the
receipt was roughly 0.6–1.0 ms and render CPU time 1.7–2.9 ms. The semantic-service
call took 20.6 ms, including 2.8 ms converting 1163 candidates into Godot values,
2.8 ms retaining a receipt, 2.9 ms accepting/copying draft rows and 8.7 ms binding
visible controls. These nested measurements must not be added together.
Unchanged terminal payloads were then converted and destroyed on every poll,
consuming roughly 6–9 ms per service call. Render-queue marker delays are not GPU
execution time; asynchronous viewport samples do not identify an exact same-frame
GPU interval. Probes perturbed frame cadence, so those frame intervals are not
normal-player acceptance results.

`poll_management_header` now polls transport and returns receipt metadata only.
After session invalidation checks, the service requests
`management_payload(epoch, revision, sequence)` only for its matching terminal
request. The getter validates all three identities against retained native state
without polling again, then returns a fresh owned Godot value. An empty result
retains the active ticket for draining; no partial payload is published. Existing
`poll_management` callers retain the full-value API. The construction observer
transfers its already-isolated candidate rows into its draft; other draft callers
keep copy-by-default behavior. Service retention and signal recipients remain
isolated. No worker, shared engine resources or frame budget was introduced.

`build/construction-phase-receipt-20261004-024147` measured receipt processing at
15.1 ms, draft acceptance at 0.64 ms and unchanged polls around 0.4 ms. Four walls
completed. Remaining one-time CPU work includes conversion, retention and visible
control binding. Temporary GDScript probes were removed; opt-in native management
profiling scopes remain.

Final unprofiled `build/construction-receipt-final-20261004-024426` measured a
largest opening interval of 21 ms, with ordinary frames mainly 16–17 ms. This
includes eight frames after readiness and excludes screenshot/export work. It
improves the previous 27–30 ms measurement below, but is not strict 60-fps
acceptance or a large-stock benchmark. Six cancel/reopen cycles and 22 strict
material clicks passed, followed by four naturally completed walls (+350 simulation
frames). Live assertions verified header payload omission and rejection of
mismatched epoch, revision and sequence.

`build/construction-furniture-clear-qa-20261004-024529` passed pending cancellation,
exact item, Last, Reports/Play and both beds' natural completion. Five headless
suites passed: semantic service, construction draft, material view, pause guard
and Reports controller. New regressions verify no payload conversion during 120
pending/idle polls, matching delivery, refused-payload retention, generation
replacement and transferred/default-copy row ownership. Logs and source hashes:
`build/notes/pm/receipt-implementation-validation.json`.

Live checks are `passed_with_known_issues` for the pinned renderer shutdown and
two-object diagnostics, with no unclassified diagnostics. Protected manifests
stayed unchanged; owned sessions ended without saving. The unexplained earlier
four-click failure below remains an evidence gap; subsequent passes do not
establish its cause. Development sources/extension are updated; packaged RC5 is
unchanged. This section preserves the measured cause and receipt ownership
contract for subsequent agents.

## Construction picker presentation cost (2026-10-04)

The material picker no longer rebuilds its full control tree on every refresh.
`construction_material_view.gd` retains a viewport-sized pool of native rows in
`construction_material_row.gd`; the complete semantic list determines scroll
extent and exact identities, while only visible rows bind widgets. Selection,
filtering, expansion and scrolling reuse those controls. Lock changes update
button state without rebinding rows. A press records its binding generation so
releasing after scrolling/recycling cannot select a different item. Hiding the
picker clears its callbacks and snapshot references. Shared styles and unchanged
palette roles avoid repeated theme propagation. These are main-thread controls,
not worker-created engine resources or a per-frame work-budget mechanism.

`ui_texture` now crops the retained CPU atlas image instead of calling
`Texture2D.get_image()` and synchronizing with the GPU. Original art is still
loaded from the supported install and cached for the asset owner's lifetime.
This does not establish that all game art fits resident in VRAM. Material icon
palette baking itself was only about 3 ms total in the initial detailed trace;
the larger problem included repeated UI creation and receipt copying.

The semantic service retains an isolated receipt and gives its last owned local
payload to the one-shot observer; it no longer makes another deep copy for that
observer. Signal delivery remains isolated and is skipped without listeners.
The construction pause guard subscribes only while draining a submitted mutation,
including an unknown result, rather than copying every material-list read while
idle. Ownership and late-receipt behavior have explicit regression coverage.

Measured ordinary-stock workload: 1163 items and 30 groups. Initial deep capture
`build/construction-hitch-baseline-20261004-014246` recorded a 91 ms opening frame;
the earlier native-integration runs measured 90–103 ms. Final unprofiled runs
`build/construction-hitch-final-repeat-20261004-021427` and
`build/construction-hitch-stress-20261004-021719` measured largest opening frames
of 27 and 30 ms respectively, with surrounding frames generally 16–17 ms.
The measurement includes eight frames after readiness, before screenshot GPU
readback. This is a substantial reduction, **not a strict 16.7 ms frame guarantee**.
Detailed profiling and screenshot/trace-export stalls are not compared as ordinary
player frames. Temporary GDScript timing wrappers were removed.

Verification:

- The repeat naturally completed four walls (+475 simulation frames). The stress
  run checked every one of 22 clicks without retries, cancelled/reopened six times,
  and naturally completed four walls (+675 frames).
- `build/construction-furniture-clear-qa-20261004-021839` passed pending cancellation,
  exact item selection, Last, Reports/Play and two beds' natural completion (+575).
- Six headless scripts passed: construction materials, semantic service, pause
  guard, construction controller, Closest and item icons. New tests cover a
  5000-item expansion without pool growth, scrolling to/selecting its final item,
  recycled press/release identity, pending locks, hidden callback retirement,
  replacement snapshots and retained/signal/observer payload isolation.
- GPU material and original-UI assertions passed. Raw logs are
  `build/notes/pm/hitch-final-*.{stdout,stderr}.log` and `hitch-gpu-*`.
  GPU/live results remain `passed_with_known_issues` for the existing pinned
  render-thread finalization/two-object shutdown diagnostics. The original-UI
  test also deliberately exercises its missing-art fallback.
- One earlier run, `build/construction-hitch-final-20261004-021204`, opened in
  26 ms but failed the harness's four-click placement assertion. It did not record
  per-click selections, so its cause remains unresolved; successful repeats do
  not erase that failure. The subsequent harness records group counts and verifies
  each click, selecting an enabled group rather than assuming the first has four
  available items. The repeat used the first group for all four successful clicks.

All owned live sessions ended without saving and preserved the protected source
manifest. The unrelated Godot editor in the pf2 project was left running. The
native bridge is unchanged by this presentation fix. Development extension/source
are updated; the existing packaged RC5 executable is unchanged. Keep the residual
frame cost and unexplained earlier QA failure visible when assessing the next RC.

Recipe builder RVA0xaae4b0 accepts a buildreq pointer; collector0xa29630 accepts a
job_item_filter and separate candidate output vector. Suitability0xa27c60 and
container gate0xc93380 are subordinate routines. The inspected bodies contain no

prove transitive safety. The collector mutates owned filter counters and may
update context-dependent burrow/stockpile fields. Both collector and suitability
can reach lazy walkable-group reader0x10afe0, so a wrapper must prove those paths

requirement construction0xa69bf0 supplies owned filters; their cleanup follows

The whole UI caller0x406170
must not be wrapped. Candidate population remains distinct from later placement
enablement and material grouping.

## Native material navigation integration (2026-10-04)

Construction material distance lookups call DF53.16's native flood through
`bridge/plugin/construction_material_native.cpp`, including connected Track.
Candidate admission, grouping, placement geometry and construction commands have
separate owners; this callback computes material-navigation distances only.

The internal distance callback accepts owned seed/target arrays and an optional
construction subtype. The unused Lua material-terrain reader chain and search
bounds/limit parameters have been removed from the callback and its callers.
The separate Track routing terrain reader remains. Developer console commands
retain their legacy trailing argument for compatibility with captured harnesses;
it does not impose a native flood work limit. Native frontier/storage limits
remain enforced by the wrapper.

Material selection has one implementation in `construction_draft.gd`. Its
`construction_exact_selection_test.gd` exercises all 558 recorded native kernel
transitions plus recorded group clicks, final reserved IDs and exact-item repeat
clicks. The test-only Lua selection copy and tests of the unused terrain reader
were removed; native evidence fixtures retain their historical provenance.

Cleanup verification (2026-10-22): bridge build/install, 76 adapter cases, 28
candidate/order cases, catalog/embedding checks and all 19 root CTest checks
passed. Godot draft and exact-selection suites passed with the known rendering
thread notice. Protected run `build/construction-native-cleanup-20261022-094556`
passed six cancel/reopen cycles, 22 material clicks and natural completion of
four walls after 425 simulation frames. Its picker capture was inspected; the
owned source manifest was unchanged and the session ended without saving.
The run is `passed_with_known_issues` for the documented rendering-thread,
render-device shutdown and two-object diagnostics. Installed development plugin
SHA256: `98ca87ae03d80d8ce20ecd7bb3b1939f0f3efc9f897349dc0b7f236a902f7605`.

The older `build/construction-acceptance-20261022-094424` run failed at the
TradeDepot material oracle: `construction-acceptance-verify.lua` still compares
squared geometric distance and tuple ties, superseded by native navigation.
Its source was preserved; that harness needs a separate oracle update and is
not a passing check. The QA gate also remains blocked by unregistered
`setup_launcher_test.gd`, `setup_mock.gd` and `setup_session_test.gd`; the focused
checks above ran directly. No full offline-gate or packaged-release pass is claimed.

The callback runs synchronously at the bridge safe point. Godot still sends and
receives asynchronous semantic requests. It validates the supported PE identity
and complete flood fingerprint plus compiled structure offsets, allocates its own
request, snapshots/restores generation/clear fields, all loaded block path costs
and both frontier buffers, then returns only owned scalar results. No native UI
request is read or driven. The supplied semantic seeds are encoded in a native
Construction rectangle/mask (one level, at most 31 by 31); construction subtypes
are passed through so DF supplies its own stair-specific vertical origins. Other
families retain their previously verified semantic footprints. Item and geometry
limits remain distinct from simulation throughput; scratch snapshots reject more
than 250000 loaded blocks and retain no pointers across calls.

Both frontier tails receive invalid-coordinate sentinels after backup. If either
last slot is written, the callback rejects all distances as ResourceLimit,
conservatively including exactly-full frontiers. RAII restores scratch on normal
and C++ exception exits. Developer reasons remain internal: overflow uses native
"Building Placement Distance Overflow" verbatim (DF string RVA 0x16bebc8), and
other native-wrapper failures have no invented player-facing substitute. The
native error text is not prefixed with authored material-list prose.

Verification and retained evidence:

- `build/native-material-integration-20261004-001427`: Wall, Floor and Bed
  comparisons matched their native pickers, including generation reset; reopened
  pickers remained identical and simulation resumed. Invalid footprint rejected.
  Development-only frontier fault injection returned ResourceLimit with no
  partial distances and restored generation state. This validates the rejection
  path, not a naturally occurring 120000-entry overflow stress case.
- `build/native-integration-stairs-reverse-20261004-000920`: all 12 stair-selection
  variants matched native distances normally and after forced generation reset.
- `build/native-integration-bridge-20261004-001011`: 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 1x3 and 3x1
  matched native distances at 2402 candidate/nearby positions each, normally and
  after reset. Nearby solid/air positions cover reachable and unreachable

- `build/connected-track-material-item-distances-20261004-001756`: four normal-build

- `build/construction-furniture-clear-qa-20261004-002139`: cancellation during

## Construction lookup performance: 0.1.0-rc.5

The maintainer authorized prioritizing explicit gameplay actions over simulation
throughput. Profiling the ordinary-stock four-wall case found navigation consumed
1438 ms of 1578 ms preparation; batching gaps were small and item details took
15 ms. Increasing the builder share alone would not address that cost.

The RC5 package used hash indexes for visited tiles and per-search facts.
Source builds use the native callback described under Native material navigation
integration; the following measurements describe the RC5 implementation.
Explicit frontier/target vectors determined traversal and output order. The Lua
fact reader shared one tile observation among its destination/opening predicates
within a synchronous call, without retaining native pointers or dynamic facts
across reads or safe points. This optimization preserved movement rules, item
eligibility, distance metrics and wire format; the viewer remained asynchronous.

The repeated live case prepared 1163 items in 30 groups in 906 ms (navigation
781 ms), about 43% less preparation time. The measured picker wait was 925 ms
versus 1621 ms in the baseline; this harness interval begins after pointer release,
not at click-down. During lookup, 95% of 58 viewer frames were at most 17 ms,
maximum 90 ms. Four walls completed naturally at +400 observed simulation frames.
These are sampled timings on this machine, not promises for every fort. A paired
reader probe produced identical facts at 11163 real tile positions. Evidence:
`build/construction-material-profile-20261003-115713` (baseline) and
`build/construction-material-profile-20261003-120445` (optimized).

An earlier optimized run (`build/construction-material-profile-20261003-120158`)
populated choices in 799 ms and placed four walls, but timed out waiting for
automatic resume. It remains an unresolved intermittent QA finding, not a passing
gameplay result or a proven startup-state issue. The repeat explicitly observes
the initial running state and captures final session/guard state. Existing
RC4/RC3/RC2 defects remain applicable. Final gameplay/package verification is
recorded in the RC5 external validation record when complete.

Opt-in diagnostics: set `dfhack.df3d_construction_profile={}` before a lookup in a
protected development lane and read its scalar rows afterward. Navigation/details
are nested intervals; do not sum them with elapsed or active time. Disable by
setting the field to nil. No timers run inside ordinary unprofiled coroutine steps.
Final furniture gameplay (`build/construction-furniture-clear-qa-20261003-121120`)
passed cancellation, exact item, Last, Reports/Play and natural completion of two
beds. All owned sessions closed without saving; live status is
`passed_with_known_issues` for the documented engine diagnostics.
Offline evidence: `build/qa/material-performance-final-core`,
`build/qa/material-performance-viewer`, native callback replay, 74 adapter
regressions and 10 terrain-reader tests. RC5 work-count coverage checked shared
observation and dynamic occupancy changes across recorded tiles.

## Busy indication and gameplay QA: 0.1.0-rc.4

RC4 adds the maintainer-requested animated activity marker to construction
material loading and placement. It is indeterminate, uses the native palette,
adds no status copy or invented percentage, and stops when choices are ready.
The explicit 2026-10-03 request authorizes this asynchronous-wait indication;
it does not loosen native-copy requirements elsewhere. Lookup latency remains.

Gameplay QA found and fixed another input defect: immediately after closing
Reports, Play could remain disabled until the next HUD refresh, losing a quick
click. UI-host ownership/gate changes now refresh HUD controls synchronously.
A regression checks enablement without waiting for another frame; paired live
input verifies that the immediate click submits Resume and DF actually runs.

New tests click the actual build-menu hierarchy and controls. A running fortress
completed four wall tiles. A paused fortress cancelled a pending lookup, placed
two beds through expanded item selection, Keep building and Last, visited Reports,
resumed, and naturally completed both beds after 600 observed simulation frames.
Furniture tests seed two beds; the wall test retains ordinary stock. A separate
running-stock test confirmed the native shortage display while the seeded bed
was already in a DF job. An occupied-site case was retained: DF suspended a bed
job with its announcement "Item blocking site." This is not counted as completed
construction; clear-floor placement completed. These are targeted QA passes,
not proof of every recipe, viewport, long-session state or gameplay system.

Evidence: `fixtures/construction/material_candidates.json` →
`busy_gameplay_qa_reference`; `build/qa/construction-busy-corrected` and

are retained, not passed off as product successes. All owned sessions closed

## Construction gameplay follow-up: 0.1.0-rc.3

RC3 fixes the running-game material picker failure reproduced against RC2.
Native DF stops simulation during material selection. DF3D now acquires a
confirmed semantic pause before material lookup and retains it through the
placement receipt. Cancellation or confirmed placement restores a previously
running fortress. A pre-existing pause, newer player/Reports pause, native
interruption, changed session or unknown command outcome prevents unsafe resume.
There are no native-widget runtime reads or replacement visible strings.
The existing two-click construction gesture is unchanged; it was not the
cause of the reproduced failure. A lost connection can leave DF paused rather
than issue an unowned resume. Picker loading remains slow: 1627 ms in the
ordinary-stock four-tile capture; the poll interval is now 50 ms instead of 250 ms.
This is an open performance defect, not a native-parity acceptance decision.

Regression evidence: `fixtures/construction/material_candidates.json`
`running_picker_reference`. Native and viewer probes use the same existing
protected source without saving. Running-game cancellation/reopening and a
single wall completed naturally; four individual material clicks placed four
walls, all naturally completed 500 simulation frames after observation began.
Live status is `passed_with_known_issues` (documented Godot shutdown diagnostics).
Targeted guard/controller/input checks and root CTest pass; the prior controller
poll-timing assertion was corrected for the new interval. Evidence is in
`build/qa/construction-running-final` and
`build/qa/construction-running-poll-correction`. The other RC2 feature evidence
below is baseline evidence, not a claim that every workflow was revalidated.

# Engineering guide

Agent-maintained reference for building, running, verifying and releasing DF3D.
`README.md` is reserved for the maintainer to write; keep technical maintenance here. Architecture
constraints and contributor rules live in [AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md](AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md),
and supported dependency builds live in [PINS.md](PINS.md).

## Project overview and current scope

DF3D is an experimental 3D frontend for Dwarf Fortress. Explore your fortress in Godot while
Dwarf Fortress runs the simulation, with DFHack connecting the two.

It has three pieces: the **bridge** (a DFHack plugin running inside Dwarf Fortress that publishes
game state), the **core** (`schema/` and `worldmodel/`, engine-independent C++), and the
**viewer** (a Godot project plus a native extension).

**Status.** Product launches own a native DF child session and render its terrain,
creatures, items and animations; pause, unpause and save remain available. The
toolbar exposes designation and inspection tools, Reports/alerts, construction
and Stockpiles, plus read-only Residents, Work Details and Work orders panels.
Zones remains staged, and other management screens are not implemented. Windows x64 packages bundle the viewer and a bridge setup launcher;
source builds are also supported. Both require the pinned Steam release of Dwarf Fortress.

## Viewer preferences

The upper-right gear opens the viewer preferences. Escape opens
this menu from normal play and closes it again; active panels, designation tools,
and captured Walk input retain their back/cancel behavior first. Holding Escape
does not repeatedly toggle the menu.

Display contains saved Windowed and desktop Borderless fullscreen modes, with
standard windowed resolution presets. Apply previews the choice; Keep changes
persists it. Revert, closing Settings or a 15-second timeout restores the previous
actual window mode, size and position. Borderless fullscreen uses desktop resolution;
windowed sizes are clamped to the current screen work area. Startup restores them
only after an explicit display selection. Automatic interface scaling (the default), manual interface scale,
targeting grid, visual style, creature scaling
and combat effects are independent. Disabled manual scale controls cannot change
the automatic preference through value-change signals. Camera contains view mode and movement speed. Audio contains
mute and the existing four volume controls. Tabs keep the menu compact, with
independently scrolling contents and a fixed Close button. Preferences continue
to use the existing presentation/audio configuration stores. This viewer-owned
surface is an explicit exception to native gameplay UI parity; it does not expose
unfinished native Options routes. F10 remains the interface recovery shortcut.

Automatic scaling uses the native default 190x64 target grid with whole-pixel
8x12-derived cells, independently of world zoom. Manual sizing supports 75-400%
and fits small windows. Existing non-default manual sizes remain manual; legacy
default-size preferences gain automatic sizing. The HUD, minimap, information,
construction, hover and inspection canvases share both scale axes. Captured native
geometry is recorded in `fixtures/hud/automatic_scale.json`; `hud_scale_test`
checks those sizes, manual input coordinates and preference persistence.

The main HUD retains native visible slots independently of route availability:
all eight information icons, Stocks, the four bottom action groups, map controls,
and military/world buttons keep their native footprint. Unfinished routes remain
inert, per the maintainer's visual-parity direction. The upper-right gear opens
DF3D Settings; the separate bottom-right Settings text button is removed. Help
remains unwired. DFHack logo/Sitemap adornments are omitted at the maintainer's
request. No extracted artwork is packaged.

`native_hud.gdshader` reconstructs each installed 8x12 UI cell independently with
bounded, byte-rounded Lanczos3 at fractional scales and nearest at integer scales.
The bitmap font keys magenta to transparent black, preserving native straight-alpha
filtering; neighboring glyphs cannot bleed into one another. Text tint is applied
before reconstruction so native colored-edge overshoot is preserved. The moon
uses a Sprite2D at physical-pixel coordinates to avoid Control rounding before
canvas scaling. One shared material
also covers arriving notifications and rebuilt tool rows. This canvas path is
independent of world color postprocessing. Protected DF53.16 evidence in
`build/notes/visual-polish/native-20261013-114704/w1920h1080.png` establishes the
1920x1080 anchors and source filtering. `build/notes/hud-fidelity/` contains the
GPU comparison and full-scene replay. The replay transcribes native header values
only in its ignored harness; product labels remain driven by session data.


## Windows package

Run `DF3D-0.1.0-windows-x64.exe`, select your installed Dwarf Fortress, and use **Set up bridge**
with the game closed. The launcher discovers Steam libraries and also accepts `DF3D_DF_PATH`
or a folder selected with Browse. Godot and the required runtimes are included.

Setup verifies file hashes and backs up replaced files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/DF3D/backups`.
**Restore bridge files** reverses setup, refusing to overwrite files changed afterward.
Extracted application files and logs are under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/DF3D`.

The release launcher starts DF and the viewer inside one Windows kill-on-close
job. It refuses to attach to an existing DF instance. Either child exiting ends
the owned session; launcher failure and partial-startup errors also clean it up.
The Settings menu includes **Exit game**, and the window close button uses the
same native DF quit-without-saving confirmation (installed frame, bitmap font and
Quit/Cancel artwork). Unsaved progress is discarded only after explicit confirmation;
known pending saves/operations disable confirmation until they settle. Exit does
not initiate a save. Abrupt process failures still terminate the owned session.
The native DF window remains available during play. Explicit developer `-Attach`
sessions retain their separate contract and never terminate an unrelated game.
Existing packaged RC5 binaries are unchanged until a new package is built.

Run `python tools/release/test_lifecycle.py` to compile and test Windows process
ownership using stand-ins: normal cleanup, failed startup, owner crash, duplicate
cleanup and unrelated-process preservation. `release_close_test` covers exit
confirmation/cancellation, pending saves and duplicate requests; `fortress_hud_test`
covers Settings. These checks do not exercise a real fortress save or certify a
new packaged release.

## Build from source

### What you need

- Git, and CMake 3.20 or later.
- MSYS2 with `mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc` and `mingw-w64-x86_64-make`: builds the core and the Godot extension.
- Visual Studio 2022 C++ build tools with the Windows SDK: builds the DFHack fork (MSVC is
  required for ABI compatibility with the game).
- Strawberry Perl with `XML::LibXML`: DFHack's df-structures code generation.
- Python 3.12: the test suite.
- Dwarf Fortress 53.16 and Godot 4.7.2 (editor build), both from Steam.
- PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) or Windows PowerShell 5.1.

The exact supported builds are listed in [PINS.md](PINS.md). DFHack and godot-cpp are pinned Git
submodules; a source ZIP does not include them.

### Get the source

Run everything below in one PowerShell session from the repository directory. The path assignments are
the standard install locations; edit them if yours differ:

```powershell
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/UncertainCat/DF3D.git
cd DF3D
$mingwBin = 'C:\msys64\mingw64\bin'
$godotExe = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Godot Engine\godot.windows.opt.tools.64.exe'
$dfPath = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Dwarf Fortress'
$env:Path = "$mingwBin;$env:Path"
```

The same paths can be set once as environment variables instead: `DF3D_DF_PATH`, `DF3D_GODOT` and
`DF3D_MINGW_BIN` are read by the viewer, the QA gate and the smoke scripts.
`Play.cmd` discovers DF and Godot across Steam libraries when paths are omitted;
`tools/build_bridge.ps1` discovers DF before installing. Explicit command-line paths take
priority over environment variables, then discovery. An invalid override fails rather than
silently selecting another installation. `DF3D_STEAM_ROOT` can select the Steam root whose
`steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf` lists your libraries.

### Build the core and viewer

The core and its tests need only Git, CMake, MSYS2 and the submodules.

```powershell
cmake -S . -B build -G "MinGW Makefiles" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

cmake -S presentations/godot/extension -B build/godot-ext -G "MinGW Makefiles" `
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo `
    "-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$mingwBin/g++.exe" `
    "-DCMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM=$mingwBin/mingw32-make.exe"
cmake --build build/godot-ext -j
& $godotExe --headless --editor --path presentations/godot/project --import --quit
```

The import step registers the extension's native classes; run it after every extension build,
with Godot closed.

### Build and install the bridge

Register DF3D as a DFHack plugin (once), then with Dwarf Fortress closed build and install the
DFHack fork and DF3D plugin into your game installation (`-SkipInstall` builds only):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force external/dfhack/plugins/external | Out-Null
'add_subdirectory("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../../../bridge/plugin" df3d-plugin)' |
    Set-Content -Encoding ascii external/dfhack/plugins/external/CMakeLists.txt
./tools/build_bridge.ps1 -DfPath $dfPath
```

## Play

With Dwarf Fortress closed, start the viewer and choose a fortress in the selector; it opens paused:

```powershell
./Play.cmd -DfPath $dfPath -GodotExe $godotExe
```

For Steam installations, `./Play.cmd` alone discovers both paths. Run
`./Play.cmd -CheckInstall` to print the resolved paths and check that the executable,
extension and bridge files exist, without starting the game or changing preferences.
This checks file presence only; version compatibility and runtime loading require the
connection check below.

This launcher starts a temporary game session on a hidden desktop. **Closing the viewer or
launcher ends that session without saving**, so save through Settings first. Sessions also end
after 120 minutes by default; pass `-MaxMinutes` to change that.

### Recovering by hand

A session rewrites `prefs/init.txt` in the Dwarf Fortress folder (backup: `prefs/init.txt.df3d-backup`)
and adds `dfhack-config/init/dfhackzzz_df3d_menu.init` (`enable df3d`), reverting both on exit.
If a session is interrupted, the next launch restores the backup unless you changed settings since.
To recover by hand, copy the backup over `prefs/init.txt` and delete the menu init file while the
game is closed.

### Attach to a running game

To use a game you have already started, run `enable df3d` in its DFHack console, then attach:

```powershell
./Play.cmd -Attach -DfPath $dfPath -GodotExe $godotExe
```

Attach mode requires exactly one running Dwarf Fortress process. It preserves the game's pause
state and leaves the game running when you close the viewer.

## Tests and known problems

Recorded mirror fixtures are stored as deterministic `.df3dfix.gz` archives with
sibling manifests under `fixtures/recorded`. The QA gate verifies their hashes,
expands them and checks every snapshot's schema before scheduling dependent tests.
Run `python tools/qa/expand_fixtures.py` before standalone fixture checks. Consumer
validation remains authoritative; the gate's bounded header check only detects
missing or incompatible recordings early.

After a breaking snapshot change, capture fresh semantic data through the protected
lane and update the archive hashes, schema, camera/clock metadata and provenance
together. Never invent missing facts to migrate an old recording. Scene tests and
smoke tools read the manifest view instead of hardcoding coordinates from an older
fortress. The paused fixture establishes replay behavior, not running-simulation,
deep-pit visibility or complete native UI acceptance.

Connected Track remains disabled. The independent world-model search and piece
planner have fixture coverage, but production terrain eligibility, semantic bridge
placement and controller integration are unfinished. Native DF behavior is the
authority; the existing generic construction validator is not suitable for Track.
Native viewscreens, buildreq and cached path state are oracle inputs only, never
runtime inputs. Carved-track runtime routing remains unchanged.

`fixtures/construction/connected_track.json` retains bounded semantic evidence and
provenance from protected DF53.16 captures; raw captures stay under ignored build
output. Accepted captures verify unchanged owned source saves. Synthetic terrain,
copied walkable groups and bounded instant-build/one-tick settling are fixture
setup, not evidence of natural construction, hauling or minecart traversal.

`wm::routeTrackPath` implements destination-seeded three-dimensional search with
native frontier ordering, the 80K frontier cap, directed edges and linked ramp/top
marking. Callers supply semantic eligibility, forward-edge and linked-tile rules
plus inclusive loaded bounds. Wider arithmetic protects int32 boundaries.
`routeFlatTrackPath` delegates with a single-level bound and rejects unequal z.
`track_path_native_fixture` compares 342 retained flat rows and 154 elevation and
directional rows, including repeated observations. Controlled fixture callbacks
do not establish general terrain eligibility. The linked-tile bookkeeping resolves
the earlier two erroneous upper-level detours; the older 18/20 scratch comparison
is diagnostic history, not the current implementation result.

`wm::trackPathPieces` converts a validated path and independent ramp terrain facts
into cardinal connections and ramp flags. `wm::planTrackConstruction` produces a
pure Create/Update/Unchanged plan without reservations or mutations. It preserves
separate expected pending-job IDs/connections/shapes and terrain connections/kind/
shape for later safe-point validation. It rejects invalid routes, duplicate or
invalid snapshots, shape conflicts and pending masks missing terrain connections.
The last condition is conservative pending native evidence. Ten native placement
cases and thirteen invalid planner inputs are covered, alongside piece validation.

Native placement evidence establishes the following controlled cases:

- Initial flat and east-facing ascending paths request four materials and create
  four jobs, including TrackRampEW on the ramp; Keep-building false returns to map.
- Pending flat or ramp crossings retain the crossing job ID, merge connections

Management protocol34 adds `ConnectedTrackOptions.destination` to construction
Preview, Place and Materials requests for `Construction:Track`. The ordinary origin
is the first point; endpoint order is preserved, including z and stationary drafts.
